إِخَاذَةٌ Land which a man, (S, L, K,) or a Sul- tán, (S, L,) takes for himself; as also ↓ إِخَاذٌ : (S, L, K:) or land which a man takes for himself, and brings into a state of cultivation after its having been waste: (AA, Mgh, L:) or waste land which the owner gives to him who shall cultivate it: (Mgh:) and land which the Imám gives to one, not being property, (K,) or not being the property of another. (TA, as from the K.) ―
-b2- See also إِخَاذٌ, in five places. ―
-b3- Also The handle of a [shield of the kind called] حَجَفَة; (K; [in the L written جحْفة, with the ج before the ح;]) also called its ثقاف. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
